title: Quiet money (batch 3): location-data brokers + quiet political-money operators
source: Public record: SEC/FEC; company histories; investigative reporting (Vice/404 Media on SafeGraph location data; ProPublica/NYT on dark-money; OpenSecrets). Catalog layer (#242). Structural overlay; person nodes carry Persons-tab dossiers. FOCUS: the low-profile ADTECH/data-broker fortunes + quiet political mega-donors who shape surveillance + policy without public visibility. HONESTY: holdings/donations/data-sales are FACT; influence/intent graded; no coordinated conspiracy imputed.

edges.notes: Auren Hoffman - serial data-broker founder (RapLeaf, LiveRamp, then SafeGraph) - the low-profile builder of the commercial location-data industry (fact).

SafeGraph sells precise foot-traffic / points-of-interest location data; drew scrutiny after selling data that could reveal visits to abortion clinics (Planned Parenthood, 2022) - the sharp edge of the location-broker market; Google banned SafeGraph from the Play Store (fact).
SafeGraph anchors the location-broker tier of the data ecosystem - wiring the quiet-money layer to the surveillance/Location_Data thread (Niantic/auto-telematics/LexisNexis) (fact).
Scott Howe - CEO of LiveRamp (formerly Acxiom) - identity-resolution + data-onboarding that links offline identities to online ad IDs; the plumbing of surveillance advertising (fact).

LiveRamp IS the renamed Acxiom (after Acxiom sold its Marketing Solutions unit to IPG, 2018) - one of the oldest, largest consumer data brokers (thousands of attributes on ~2.5B people) rebranded around identity resolution (fact).
Acxiom/LiveRamp is the archetypal mass consumer-data broker - the 'default' example in FTC data-broker reports (fact).
LiveRamp + LexisNexis Risk Solutions are the two poles of the identity/data-broker world (marketing vs risk/policing) - both descend from decades of record-aggregation (fact).

Farris + Dan Wilks - fracking billionaires (sold Frac Tech, 2011) turned quiet Christian-right mega-donors (Ted Cruz super PAC, Club for Growth) - low public profile, large political footprint (fact).
The Wilkses fund conservative/Christian-right causes partly through pooled dark-money vehicles - the quiet-donor model (fact of category; specific flows partly opaque).
Richard Uihlein - co-founder of Uline (shipping/packaging; privately held) - with wife Liz among the very largest, lowest-profile GOP/hard-right donors (fact).
The Uihleins are the top funders of the Club for Growth + numerous hard-right candidates/causes (election-integrity groups, Tea Party legacy) - quiet but pivotal (fact).
Uihlein money also flows through DonorsTrust-style conduits - the donor-advised 'dark-money ATM' of the right (fact of vehicle use; amounts partly opaque).

DonorsTrust - the donor-advised fund known as the right's 'dark-money ATM' - channels anonymous money to conservative legal/policy orgs incl. the Leo/Federalist-Society network - wiring the quiet-donor layer to the judiciary thread (#208) (fact).
Thomas Peterffy - founder of Interactive Brokers (pioneered electronic market-making); Florida's richest, low-profile, and a large GOP donor (fact).
Peterffy is a major (quiet) donor to Republican/free-market causes - the self-made-immigrant-turned-libertarian-megadonor profile (fact).

David Siegel - co-founder of Two Sigma (with John Overdeck); completes the quant-data-fund pair; a low-profile computer-scientist billionaire (a rare public governance feud with Overdeck aside) (fact).

Charles Koch - Koch Industries (2nd-largest US private company) - built the most sophisticated quiet political-influence machine (Stand Together, Americans for Prosperity, the seminars/donor network) over decades (fact).
The Koch donor network historically routed large sums through DonorsTrust + affiliated 501c4s - the template for anonymized political spending at scale (fact).

The Koch network + the Leo/Federalist-Society legal movement are allied (if distinct) pillars of the conservative infrastructure - overlapping funders, aligned goals (fact of alliance; not a single org).
Koch-aligned + Club-for-Growth free-market politics overlap heavily - the libertarian-right donor ecosystem (fact of overlap).

Len Blavatnik - Access Industries (Warner Music, chemicals, tech/VC via Access); Soviet-born US-UK dual citizen; one of the wealthiest + most cross-border donors (both US parties + UK + universities) - his Soviet-privatization-era wealth origin draws recurring scrutiny (fact; origin-scrutiny graded).

Blavatnik's giving is famously bipartisan + INSTITUTION-focused (the Oxford Blavatnik School of Government; Harvard Life Lab; Yale; Tel Aviv; museums; both US parties) - a 'buy access + prestige everywhere' model distinct from the ideological-right donors above; wires the quiet-money layer to the academia catalog (fact; motive interpretation).
